verses.zh: 约阿施登基的时候年七岁，在耶路撒冷作王四十年。他母亲名叫西比亚，是别是巴人。
verses.en: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign. He reigned for forty years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother[NOTE:2] was Zibiah, who was from Beer Sheba.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “the name of his mother.”
verses.commentary:
24:1 "Joash" In 2 Kgs. 11:21; 12:1-21, he is called "Jehoash." Both mean "YWHW supports (BDB 219).

"he reigned forty years in Jerusalem" This is one of the longest reigns besides Manasseh. The tragic pattern of
initial godliness (2 Chr. 24:2) followed by end-of-life rebellion continues. As long as Jehoiada the priest was alive things
went well (i.e., v. 12).

verses.zh: 祭司耶何耶大在世的时候，约阿施行耶和华眼中看为正的事。
verses.en: Joash did what the Lord approved[NOTE:1] throughout the lifetime[NOTE:2] of Jehoiada the priest.
notes: Heb “and Joash did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord.”
Heb “all the days of.”
verses.commentary:
24:2 "did what was right in the sight of the Lord" This is an idiomatic expression
for the kings of Judah (and possibly of Israel, i.e., Jeroboam I) who acted faithfully, like David (1 Kgs. 15:3) in keeping and
promoting obedience to the Mosaic Law (cf. Deut. 6:16-18; 12:28; 13:18).

- Jeroboam I of Israel ‒ condition of YHWH's blessing: obedience to His covenant ‒ 1 Kgs. 11:33,38; 14:8, but he did not

- Asa (initially) ‒ 1 Kgs. 15:11; 2 Chr. 14:2

- Jehoshaphat (mostly) ‒ 1 Kgs. 22:43; 2 Chr. 20:32

- Jehu ‒ 2 Kgs. 10:30

- Jehoash (initially) ‒ 2 Kgs. 12:2

- Joash (initially) ‒ 2 Chr. 24:2

- Amaziah ‒ 2 Kgs. 14:2; 2 Chr. 25:2

- Jotham ‒ 2 Kgs. 15:33; 2 Chr. 27:2

- Ahaz ‒ 2 Kgs. 16:2; 2 Chr. 28:1 (negative)

- Hezekiah ‒ 2 Kgs. 18:3; 2 Chr. 29:2; 31:20

- Josiah ‒ 2 Kgs. 22:2

verses.zh: 耶何耶大为他娶了两个妻，并且生儿养女。
verses.en: Jehoiada chose two wives for him who gave him sons and daughters.
verses.commentary:
24:3 The godly High Priest, Jehoiada (cf. 2 Chr. 24:6, i.e., "head") chose wives for the young king. Although the text
does not give any details, one assumes

- they were not of the line of Ahab (i.e., Jezebel and Athaliah)

- they were worshipers of YHWH from Judah

- the text does not mention additional wives or concubines

One of the two wives is named in 2 Chr. 25:1.

verses.zh: 此后，约阿施有意重修耶和华的殿，
verses.en: Later, Joash was determined to repair the Lord’s temple.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and it was, later, there was with the heart of Joash to repair the house of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
24:4 YHWH's temple had deteriorated from non-use and the ransacking and theft by Athaliah's people (cf. 2 Chr. 24:7).

The purpose of restoration was the restart of YHWH's worship in its Mosaic form (i.e.., 2 Chr. 24:5,6,9).

verses.zh: 便召聚众祭司和利未人，吩咐他们说：「你们要往犹大各城去，使以色列众人捐纳银子，每年可以修理你们　神的殿；你们要急速办理这事。」只是利未人不急速办理。
verses.en: He assembled the priests and Levites and ordered them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and collect the annual quota of silver from all Israel for repairs on the temple of your God. Be quick about it!” But the Levites delayed.
verses.commentary:
24:5 "cities of Judah. . .all Israel" It is obvious that the Chronicler considered Judah to be the true covenant people,
"Israel" (cf. vv. 9,16).

The NASB Study Bible, p. 613, mentions that

- this verse only mentions one source of revenue (i.e., the census tax, cf. Exod. 30:14; 38:26)

- 2 Kgs. 12:4-5 lists three sources

- a census tax (i.e., "each man's assessment")

- freewill offering (i.e., "which any man's heart prompts him," cf. Exod. 35:5,22,29)

- payments from personal vows (cf. Lev. 27:1-8; Num. 18:15-16)

"But the Levites did not act quickly" The reason for the delay is not stated but from the context, one wonders if they,
too, had become followers of Ba'al. They had allowed YHWH's temple to be ransacked and looted.

The other option is the parallel in 2 Kgs. 12:6-8 which mentions the date of the request, which may denote
a time when Jehoiada had little influence (NASB Study Bible, p. 613).

A third option is expressed by Josephus, Antiq. 9.8.2., "but the high priest did not do this, as concluding
that no one would willingly pay the money."

verses.zh: 王召了大祭司耶何耶大来，对他说：「从前耶和华的仆人摩西，为法柜的帐幕与以色列会众所定的捐项，你为何不叫利未人照这例从犹大和耶路撒冷带来作殿的费用呢？
verses.en: So the king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest,[NOTE:1] and said to him, “Why have you not made[NOTE:2] the Levites collect[NOTE:3] from Judah and Jerusalem the tax authorized by Moses the Lord’s servant and by the assembly of Israel at the tent containing the tablets of the law?”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Jehoiada the head”; the word “priest” not in the Hebrew text but is implied.
Heb “demanded of.”
Heb “to bring.”
Heb “the tent of testimony.”
verses.commentary:
24:6 Joash wants to restore Mosaic guidelines for the sacrificial system.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICES IN MESOPOTAMIA AND ISRAEL AND THEIR SIGNIFICANCE

"the levy fixed by Moses" See Exod. 30:12-16.

"the servant of the Lord" In 2 Chr. 24:9 this is changed to "the servant of God."
The Chronicler must have viewed these as synonymous statements.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

"the tent of testimony" This is one of several titles for the tabernacle of the wilderness (i.e., Num. 1:50).

The "testimony" would be the two tablets of stone commandments given to Moses by God on Mt. Sinai/Horeb.

verses.zh: （因为那恶妇亚她利雅的众子曾拆毁　神的殿，又用耶和华殿中分别为圣的物供奉巴力。）
verses.en: (Wicked Athaliah and her sons had broken into God’s temple and used all the holy items of the Lord’s temple in their worship of the Baals.)
verses.commentary:
24:7 This verse reveals the people's continuing worship of Ba'al and Asherah. Notice the recurrent elements.

- There was a temple and priesthood to Ba'al in Jerusalem, 2 Chr. 23:17.

- Followers (lit. "sons") of Athaliah invaded the temple of YHWH and took some holy things to Ba'al's temple, 2 Chr. 24:7.

- The people returned to Ba'al worship even after the temple of YHWH was restored, 2 Chr. 24:18.

"the Baals" The reason Ba'al is plural is because every village and high place (naturally raised place) had its
own Ba'al and Asherah shrine. Ba'al was symbolized by an uplifted, elongated stone and Asherah by a
live tree or carved stake, symbolizing the tree of life.

verses.zh: 于是王下令，众人做了一柜，放在耶和华殿的门外，
verses.en: The king ordered a chest to be made and placed outside the gate of the Lord’s temple.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the king said [it] and they made a chest and placed it in the gate of the house of the Lord outside.”
verses.commentary:
24:8 "set it outside by the gate of the house of the Lord" This would be where all the
Judeans could place their offerings. 2 Kings 12:9 says it was placed next to the altar of sacrifice, which would limit access to
the priest and Levites. 2 Chronicles makes more sense. Obviously Kings and Chronicles have their own unique sources.

verses.zh: 又通告犹大和耶路撒冷的百姓，要将　神仆人摩西在旷野所吩咐以色列人的捐项给耶和华送来。
verses.en: An edict was sent throughout Judah and Jerusalem requiring the people to bring to the Lord the tax that Moses, God’s servant, imposed on Israel in the wilderness.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they gave voice in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the Lord the tax of Moses the servant of God upon Israel in the wilderness.”

verses.zh: 众首领和百姓都欢欢喜喜地将银子送来，投入柜中，直到捐完。
verses.en: All the officials and all the people gladly brought their silver and threw it into the chest until it was full.
verses.commentary:
24:10 This verse is surprising because in 2 Chr. 24:18 the people revert to Ba'al worship. Either there was a
group of faithful followers all along or the whole population was religiously fickle.

"the people rejoiced. . .dropped" Here is a good example of how context determines meaning. Words have meaning
only in a context (i.e., sentence, paragraph). The VERB (BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil
IMPERFECT with waw) usually means "throw," but here, "dropped" fits best. Their giving was a joy not
a burden to be resented.

verses.zh: 利未人见银子多了，就把柜抬到王所派的司事面前；王的书记和大祭司的属员来将柜倒空，仍放在原处。日日都是这样，积蓄的银子甚多。
verses.en: Whenever the Levites brought the chest to the royal accountant and they saw there was a lot of silver, the royal scribe and the accountant of the high priest emptied the chest and then took it back to its place. They went through this routine every day and collected a large amount of silver.
verses.commentary:
24:11 The large amount of money collected in the chest was not tallied nor dispensed by the Levites but by several
special leaders only.

- King's scribe

- High Priest's officer

The reason is never stated. It may relate to

- 2 Chr. 24:5, "they did not act quickly"

- 2 Chr. 24:17-18, bad counselors and a return to Ba'al worship

"the king's scribe" Kings uses royal documents often but Chronicles uses prophetic writings more often.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SCRIBES

verses.zh: 王与耶何耶大将银子交给耶和华殿里办事的人，他们就雇了石匠、木匠重修耶和华的殿，又雇了铁匠、铜匠修理耶和华的殿。
verses.en: The king and Jehoiada gave it to the construction foremen[NOTE:1] assigned to the Lord’s temple. They hired carpenters and craftsmen to repair the Lord’s temple, as well as those skilled in working with iron and bronze to restore the Lord’s temple.
notes: Heb “doers of the work.”
verses.commentary:
24:12-14 Notice the different metals used. See parallel in 2 Kgs. 12:13.

- iron, 2 Chr. 24:12 (probably for support, i.e., "strengthened it," v. 13)

- bronze, 2 Chr. 24:12 (for the sacrificial altar)

- gold, 2 Chr. 24:14 (for the Holy of Holies and Holy Place)

- silver, 2 Chr. 24:14 (for the Holy Place)

verses.zh: 工人操作，渐渐修成，将　神殿修造得与从前一样，而且甚是坚固。
verses.en: They worked hard and made the repairs.[NOTE:1] They followed the measurements specified for God’s temple and restored it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the doers of the work worked, and the repairs went up for the work by their hand.”
Heb “and they caused the house of God to stand according to its measurements and they strengthened it.”
verses.commentary: 24:13 "according to its specifications" This meant the guidelines from King David and King Solomon.

verses.zh: 工程完了，他们就把其余的银子拿到王与耶何耶大面前，用以制造耶和华殿供奉所用的器皿和调羹，并金银的器皿。耶何耶大在世的时候，众人常在耶和华殿里献燔祭。
verses.en: When they were finished, they brought the rest of the silver to the king and Jehoiada. They used it to make items for the Lord’s temple, including items used in the temple service and for burnt sacrifices, pans, and various other gold and silver items. Throughout Jehoiada’s lifetime, burnt sacrifices were offered regularly in the Lord’s temple.
verses.commentary:
24:14 "utensils" Apparently most of the sacred utensils had been stolen and taken to the temple of Ba'al
in Jerusalem (cf. 2 Chr. 23:17; 24:7).

verses.zh: 耶何耶大年纪老迈，日子满足而死。死的时候年一百三十岁，
verses.en: Jehoiada grew old and died at the age of 130.
verses.commentary:
24:15 Death was not seen as an enemy. The time of death was the concern. Life taken early, violently or by sickness,
was seen as the problem.

verses.zh: 葬在大卫城列王的坟墓里；因为他在以色列人中行善，又事奉　神，修理　神的殿。
verses.en: He was buried in the City of David[NOTE:1] with the kings, because he had accomplished good in Israel and for God and his temple.
notes: The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
verses.commentary: 24:16 This priest was buried among the kings in Jerusalem because of his faithful, life-long service.

verses.zh: 耶何耶大死后，犹大的众首领来朝拜王；王就听从他们。
verses.en: After Jehoiada died, the officials of Judah visited the king and declared their loyalty to him.[NOTE:1] The king listened to their advice.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “came and bowed down to the king.”
Heb “to them.”
verses.commentary:
24:17 This shows

- the problem of faithless counselors

- the people's devotion to Ba'al (cf. 2 Kgs. 12:3)

Joash listened to them, as he had previously listened to Jehoiada. It shows his weak personality.

verses.zh: 他们离弃耶和华―他们列祖　神的殿，去事奉亚舍拉和偶像；因他们这罪，就有忿怒临到犹大和耶路撒冷。
verses.en: They abandoned the temple of the Lord God of their ancestors[NOTE:1] and worshiped[NOTE:2] the Asherah poles and idols. Because of this sinful activity, God was angry with Judah and Jerusalem.
notes: Heb “fathers” (also in v. 24).
Heb “served.”
verses.commentary:
24:18 Again, the Chronicler asserts that judgment came because of disobedience to YHWH's covenant.

YHWH wanted to bless His people as a witness to the world but because of the curses involved in
"the two ways" (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30; Psalm 1; Proverbs 1), only judgment was seen.

The Chronicler saw all history in YHWH's hand. Judgment (temporal) was meant to turn His people
back to Him (cf. 2 Chr. 24:19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

verses.zh: 但　神仍遣先知到他们那里，引导他们归向耶和华。这先知警戒他们，他们却不肯听。
verses.en: The Lord sent prophets among them to lead them back to him.[NOTE:1] They warned[NOTE:2] the people, but they would not pay attention.
notes: Heb “and he sent among them prophets to bring them back to the Lord.”
Heb “testified among.”
verses.commentary:
24:19 "He sent prophets" Prophets, their message, and their writings were very important to the Chronicler!

YHWH had not abandoned His people. They just would not listen (cf. Isa. 6:9-13).

See Gordon Fee and Douglas Stuart, How to Read the Bible for All Its Worth, pp. 184-189.

verses.zh: 那时，　神的灵感动祭司耶何耶大的儿子撒迦利亚，他就站在上面对民说：「　神如此说：你们为何干犯耶和华的诫命，以致不得亨通呢？因为你们离弃耶和华，所以他也离弃你们。」
verses.en: God’s Spirit energized[NOTE:1] Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood up before the people and said to them, “This is what God says: ‘Why are you violating the commands of the Lord? You will not be prosperous. Because you have rejected the Lord, he has rejected you!’”
notes: Heb “clothed.”
verses.commentary:
24:20 "the Spirit of God came on" This is literally "clothed" (BDB 527, KB 519, Qal PERFECT,
cf. Jdgs. 6:34; 1 Chr. 12:18). See full note at 2 Chr. 20:14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION VS. HUMAN FREE WILL

verses.zh: 众民同心谋害撒迦利亚，就照王的吩咐，在耶和华殿的院内用石头打死他。
verses.en: They plotted against him and by royal decree stoned him to death in the courtyard of the Lord’s temple.
verses.commentary:
24:21-22 This is so shocking. Resistence to God's word blinded their minds to the service of Jehoiada and
his family. They

- conspired (BDB 905, KB 1153, Qal IMPERFECT with waw; "plot to kill," cf.
1 Sam. 22:8,13; 1 Kgs. 15:27; 16:9; 2 Kgs. 10:9; 15:10,25; 21:23,24; 2 Chr. 33:24-25)

- stoned him

- in the court of the Lord (i.e., a holy place, cf. 2 Chr. 23:14)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEATH PENALTY IN ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: STONE TO DEATH

24:21 This murder is mentioned by Jesus in Matt. 23:35; Luke 11:51.

There is some confusion over the name of the father.

- Zechariah of 2 Chronicles, father is Jehoiada

- Zechariah, the writer of canonical book, Zechariah's father is Berechiah

Luke 11:51 does not give the father's name.

If "Abel" was the first, then the second reference should be the last. This does not fit 2 Chronicles 24 well.
We do not know how, where, or when Zechariah, son of Berechiah, died, but he is a better option for a late death. See Gleason
Archer, Encyclopedia of Bible Difficulties, pp. 337-338.

verses.zh: 这样，约阿施王不想念撒迦利亚的父亲耶何耶大向自己所施的恩，杀了他的儿子。撒迦利亚临死的时候说：「愿耶和华鉴察伸冤！」
verses.en: King Joash disregarded[NOTE:1] the loyalty Zechariah’s father Jehoiada had shown him and killed Jehoiada’s[NOTE:2] son. As Zechariah[NOTE:3] was dying, he said, “May the Lord take notice and seek vengeance!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “did not remember.”
Heb “his”; the referent (Jehoiada) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (Zechariah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and seek [—].” The direct object of “seek” is omitted in the Hebrew text but implied; “vengeance” is supplied for clarification.
verses.commentary:
24:22 "May the Lord see and avenge!" The "he" must refer to Zechariah, the son of
Jehoiada.

This phrase has two IMPERFECTS used as JUSSIVES. They are a prayer
to YHWH. The VERB (BDB 205, KB 233, Qal IMPERFECT) is "seek" with no stated
object. Instead of YHWH's people "seeking" Him, He will seek them for judgment!

verses.zh: 满了一年，亚兰的军兵上来攻击约阿施，来到犹大和耶路撒冷，杀了民中的众首领，将所掠的财货送到大马士革王那里。
verses.en: At the beginning[NOTE:1] of the year the Syrian army attacked[NOTE:2] Joash[NOTE:3] and invaded Judah and Jerusalem. They wiped out all the leaders of the people and sent all the plunder they gathered to the king of Damascus.
notes: Heb “turning.”
Heb “went up against.”
Heb “him”; the referent (Joash) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
24:23-26 These verses record how the curse of 2 Chr. 24:22 was fulfilled.

- the Syrians invaded with a small force

- killed all officials (same title as 2 Chr. 24:17)

- took all the spoil of Jerusalem to Damascus (cf. 2 Kgs. 12:18)

- Joash was sickened or wounded (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 142, #6)

- Joash's foreign servants (2 Chr. 24:26; names different in 2 Kgs. 12:21) "conspired" against him and killed him
("beware of foreigners" was surely a concern of the small post-exilic Judah of the Chronicler's day)

- he was not buried in the royal tombs

verses.zh: 亚兰的军兵虽来了一小队，耶和华却将大队的军兵交在他们手里，是因犹大人离弃耶和华―他们列祖的　神，所以藉亚兰人惩罚约阿施。
verses.en: Even though the invading Syrian army was relatively weak, the Lord handed over to them Judah’s very large army,[NOTE:1] for the people of Judah[NOTE:2] had abandoned the Lord God of their ancestors. The Syrians[NOTE:3] gave Joash what he deserved.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “though with a small amount of men the army of Aram came, the Lord gave into their hand an army [that was] very large.”
Heb “they”; the referent (the people of Judah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “they”; the referent (the Syrians) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “executed judgments on Joash.”

verses.zh: 亚兰人离开约阿施的时候，他患重病；臣仆背叛他，要报祭司耶何耶大儿子流血之仇，杀他在床上，葬他在大卫城，只是不葬在列王的坟墓里。
verses.en: When they withdrew, they left Joash[NOTE:1] badly wounded. His servants plotted against him because of what he had done to[NOTE:2] the son[NOTE:3] of Jehoiada the priest. They murdered him on his bed. Thus[NOTE:4] he died and was buried in the City of David,[NOTE:5] but not in the tombs of the kings.
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (Joash) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “because of the shed blood of.”
The MT has the plural בְּנֵי (bene, “sons”), but the final yod is dittographic. Note the yod that immediately follows.
Heb “and he died.”
The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
verses.commentary:
24:25 Again, the Chronicler explains historical events in light of the "two ways" (see note at 2 Chr. 24:18).

"sons" The MT is PLURAL (also Peshitta). Possibly the people tried to wipe out the whole family.
The LXX has "son," followed by the Vulgate.

"murdered him on his bed" It is hard to reconcile the account here with the parallel in 2 Kgs. 12:20. See John H. Walton
and D. Brent Sandy, The Lost World of Scripture, which documents how oral cultures passed down their traditions. Here, it
seems to be two written sources which differ.

verses.zh: 背叛他的是亚扪妇人示米押的儿子撒拔和摩押妇人示米利的儿子约萨拔。
verses.en: The conspirators were Zabad son of Shimeath (an Ammonite woman) and Jehozabad son of Shimrith (a Moabite woman).

verses.zh: 至于他的众子和他所受的警戒，并他重修　神殿的事，都写在列王的传上。他儿子亚玛谢接续他作王。
verses.en: The list of Joash’s[NOTE:1] sons, the many prophetic oracles about him, and the account of his building project on God’s temple are included in the record of the Scroll of the Kings.[NOTE:2] His son Amaziah replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (Joash) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and the founding of the house of God, look, they are written on the writing of the scroll of the kings?”
verses.commentary:
24:27 Usually the written records used by the Chronicler are prophetic writings (i.e., 2 Chr. 13:22), but here, royal archives.
See Introduction, IV. Authorship, #2.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why did the Levites not act quickly to repair the temple?

- Why did the temple need repair?

- Why is 2 Chr. 24:18 so shocking?

- What does "the Spirit clothed Zechariah" mean?

- How was Joash killed?
